I'm researching a specific technical question for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Confluence space key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net). A team member named Kiera asked a colleague (nickname "Angelo") whether there's a planned "out of the box" (i.e. pre-built third-party library, not custom-built) solution for a calendar/date-picker component shown in a specific Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937). The screenshot shows: a "Find in Boutique" panel/flyout, with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" section with a full month calendar grid (June 2026, showing all days of the month, one date highlighted/selected), an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with clickable time slot buttons (9:00AM through 4:00PM), and a "CONTINUE" button at the bottom. The Figma layers panel shows this sits under a "Find in Boutique" grouping alongside other layers like "FIND IN BOUTIQUE modal open" variants.

Important context/discrepancy I've already found in the local repo's requirement docs (.docs/prd/*.md and .docs/integration/*.md):
- "Find in Boutique" is documented as a stock/inventory-check flyout only — it shows per-boutique product availability for a selected product+size via a MuleSoft call, using Google Maps + geolocation (PDP §8, CAI-037–042, PRD-028–039, OM-031). Nothing in its documented spec involves a calendar, date picker, or appointment time slots.
- Booxi (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor) is the actual system that handles appointments, but the current confirmed PWA scope for Booxi (CRM-165–167) is READ-ONLY appointment history display in My Account only — appointment creation/booking is explicitly documented as "not in current PWA scope... handled in Booxi's own surfaces," with storefront booking scope/timeline still "TBC" (to be confirmed).
- So a date+time-slot BOOKING calendar doesn't cleanly match either documented feature as currently scoped — it could mean the docs are stale/outdated, or this represents a scope expansion (in-storefront Booxi booking now confirmed?) that hasn't been written back into the local integration doc yet, or it's a different/new feature not yet documented locally at all (e.g. a private styling appointment, personal shopping, or "reserve to view in store" feature).
- Also: no calendar or date-picker npm package is installed in package.json at all currently, and there's no existing calendar-related code anywhere in the codebase — so if a decision on an "out of the box" library was made, it hasn't been implemented in code yet, meaning any record of the decision would only exist in Confluence or Jira.
- One more related data point: the PRD also separately documents a gift-card delivery date picker (giftcards.md, GC-005/GC-006) — "calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today" — a DIFFERENT feature that also needs a calendar UI. If the team already evaluated/chose a calendar library for that, it might be the same one intended for reuse here — worth checking too.

Please research Confluence (space SFCC) and report back on:

1. **Does Booxi's in-storefront booking scope look more confirmed/expanded in Confluence than the local docs suggest?** Search for "Booxi" pages beyond what a prior pass found (integration register, TSDs). Check if there's a newer/updated Booxi TSD, spike, or requirements page that confirms in-storefront appointment booking (not just history) is now in scope. Also check the CRM-165/166/167 requirement rows directly if you can find the source requirements sheet or its Confluence mirror.

2. **Is there a technical decision, spike, or evaluation doc about a calendar/date-picker component specifically?** Search broadly: "calendar", "date picker", "datepicker", "react-day-picker", "react-datepicker", "react-calendar", "flatpickr", "react-dates", "MUI date", "Chakra date", "out of the box". Also check whether Development Standards (261750785) or Component Override Strategy (261881857) or the newer "04.7 Component Inventory" (400195591)/"04.71 Writing User Stories for Components" (400195600) pages mention a calendar/date component or name a specific library.

3. **Is there a page specifically about "Find in Boutique"?** Search for it directly — check if Confluence's version of this feature's spec differs from (or is more current than) the local .docs/prd/pdp.md and .docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md descriptions I summarized above. Does Confluence show it including a booking/appointment step, or purely a stock-check flyout as the local docs say?

4. **Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/006)** — search for any Confluence page (requirements sheet mirror, TSD, or spike) discussing the gift card scheduled-delivery calendar UI and whether a specific library/approach was chosen for it.

5. **Any Figma-adjacent tech notes** — check if there's a "Web Design (UX)" or Design Tracker page, or any dev-handoff/tech-feasibility notes, that references this specific Figma frame/flow (a boutique appointment booking calendar with "Choose a Date" + "Available Times" + Continue) and names an implementation approach.

Report back with page titles, IDs, last-modified info, and concrete content summaries/quotes for each question — I need to know definitively whether an "out of the box" calendar solution was actually decided, and if so which one, or whether this is genuinely still an open/undecided question (in which case say so clearly rather than guessing). This is read-only research — do not create, edit, or comment on any Confluence content. Keep the report focused and organized under the 5 numbered questions; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing an answer, not an end user directly.

Research complete. Summary below, organized by the five numbered questions. All findings are read-only — no Confluence content was created, edited, or commented on.

## Cross-cutting note before the detail

Every page fetched returned empty `created`/`updated` timestamp fields from the API (a tool/data limitation, not something I can work around) — so I'm reporting **version numbers** (a proxy for edit history) and content-internal dates (e.g., "downloaded July 3rd, 2026," "Last updated 2026-07-16") where available, instead of true last-modified timestamps.

Also worth flagging up front: Confluence itself is **inconsistent on the vendor's name** — some pages call it "Booksy," others "Booxi," one page hedges with "Booksy / Booxi" together. This isn't a scope signal, just an unresolved naming inconsistency in the client's own source documents that mirrors what you already found locally.

---

## Q1 — Is Booxi's in-storefront booking scope more confirmed/expanded in Confluence?

**No — if anything it's confirmed narrower and more explicit than "maybe expanded."**

- **"Integration Reconciliation — Working Doc (Pre-Jira)"** (id `307134467`, DRAFT status, compiled 2026-07-07) is a reconciliation of all integration sources and states explicitly: *"Booxi | ✅ (in architecture.md) | — (missing from tracker) | ✅ (4 items in openItems.md) | **— not in register at all** | ... Confluence register has no page/row for Booxi."* It lists Booxi among **"Six repo integrations have no Confluence register page at all: Booxi, Transperfect, Google reCAPTCHA, GDPR cartridge, Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg."** No dedicated Booxi TSD, spike, or register page exists anywhere in the space.
- The **confirmed functional requirements** (id `302022672`, "04.1.11 Customers, Account, CRM Sync," sourced from the Zimmermann Functional Requirements Excel downloaded July 3, 2026) are unambiguous:
  - **CRM-165**: "The system will display the customer's appointment history within My Account, sourced via the Booksy API" — Status: **Confirmed**
  - **CRM-166**: "The system will treat Booksy as the system of record for all appointment data" — Status: **Confirmed**
  - **CRM-167**: "The system will accommodate appointments as a section within the My Account area so that it can be incorporated without structural redesign when ready" — Status: **Confirmed**
  - None of the three mention booking, scheduling, or creating an appointment — only display of existing history.
- **"Technical Solution Design – PWA"** (id `256835585`, v11, "Last updated 2026-07-16") is internally inconsistent in wording but resolves the same way: one summary row says *"Booxi | Boutique appointment **booking** (My Account; CRM-165–167)"*, but the more precise per-integration timeout table in the same doc says *"`booxi` | Booxi base URL **(TBD)** | Boutique appointment **read** in My Account (CRM-165–167) | ... My Account only; non-critical-path within that page."* Both cite the same CRM-165–167 IDs, and Booxi's base URL is still literally TBD.
- **"04.2 Design Tracker"** (id `258801666`) row 13, "Customer Account & CRM" → "Loyalty & Appointments" ("Loyalty page (legacy VIC); loyalty page (new Friend/Muse/Icon); Appointments (Booksy)") shows **Sprint 4, Design Status PENDING, Zimmermann Sign-off PENDING, no Figma link populated**. Per **"1.5 Web Design (UX)"** (id `268075023`), this whole area falls under **Phase 2 (account & loyalty surfaces)**, which the sign-off tracker marks **DRAFT — "Not ready for build."**
- **Important new find**: **"Store Details"** integration register (id `258441217`) documents the *only* confirmed mechanism for actually **booking** an appointment today: **INT-027, Inside Chat** — *"Live chat widget available on Store Detail page for click-and-collect queries and boutique appointment booking."* Status: Under Review. I.e., the currently-documented booking path is a **human chat handoff**, not a self-service calendar.
- **"1.4 Third Party Overview"** (id `261849101`) hedges at a summary level: *"Booxi | Boutique appointment history in My Account **(scope TBC)**"* — even though the underlying CRM-165–167 rows say Confirmed. This is an internal Confluence inconsistency, not evidence of expansion.

**Verdict**: No evidence anywhere in Confluence of in-storefront self-service booking being confirmed scope. Every source narrows to read-only history, not-yet-signed-off design, and a live-chat-based booking workaround.

---

## Q2 — Is there a technical decision/spike/evaluation about a calendar/date-picker component?

**No such document exists. This is a genuinely open/undecided question.**

- Broad searches for "calendar," "date picker," "datepicker," "react-day-picker," "react-datepicker," "react-calendar," "flatpickr," "react-dates," "MUI date," "Chakra date," and "out of the box" + component library returned nothing relevant beyond generic uses of the word "date" (meeting dates, sprint dates) and the GC-005/006 requirement text itself.
- **"04.7 Component Inventory"** (id `400195591`, v13) — the design system's own catalogue — lists Banner, Button, Icon Button, Checkbox & Radio, Footer, Disclaimer, Textfield, Dropdown, Link, Logo Masthead, Navigation, Title and Link, Cart Item, Editorial Cards, PDP Hero, Product Card Base/Group, Recently Viewed. **No Calendar or DatePicker component is listed anywhere.**
- **"04.71 Writing User Stories for Components"** (id `400195600`) is a generic process guide (Level 1 component epics vs. Level 2 page epics) with no calendar-specific content.
- The architecture TSD's only UI-library statement is generic: *"UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme tokens"* — no calendar/date npm package named anywhere.
- No page or comment mentions "Kiera," and no page references the Figma node-id `3193-47937` or `node-id=3193` directly.

**Verdict**: If Kiera and Angelo's conversation happened, it was not written back into Confluence anywhere I could find (no matching page, no matching comment on any page checked, including the Design Tracker, the CRM/Appointments page, Store Details, and the Gift Cards page — all returned zero comments).

## Q3 — Is there a page specifically about "Find in Boutique"? Does it include a booking step?

**No page is titled exactly "Find in Boutique," but it's thoroughly documented elsewhere, and it never includes a booking/calendar step.**

- **"Find In Store — Boutique Stock Availability"** (id `292487173`) is the MuleSoft-level technical design (JIRA ZMOBLD-218, Technical Owner Surya Veer). Its request/response contract is literally just `{"ProductId": "2350275", "CountryCode": "GB"}` → `[{"StoreId": "...", "qty": 1}]`. **No date/time field exists anywhere in this API.**
- Functional requirements PRD-018, PRD-028–039 (id `302776322`, "04.1.8 Product, Catalogue and PDP"), the CAI section (id `302415874`, "04.1.5 Cart and Inventory"), and the Order Management section (id `303464449`) all describe Find in Boutique identically: PDP/Cart CTA → side-out/modal with product thumbnail+name+colour+price → size selector → location search + "Use My Location" geolocation → Google Maps directions → results list (name, address, distance, stock status In Stock/Low Stock/Out of Stock, plus per a PRD-035 comment: opening hours, contact details, live open/closed status, map, "view more" button) → Enter-key search, configurable result limit, fully responsive.
- This matches your local `.docs/prd/pdp.md` / `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md` summary exactly — both are sourced from the same "Zimmermann Functional Requirements" Excel, downloaded July 3, 2026.

**Verdict**: Confluence confirms, does not contradict, the local docs. No calendar, date, or appointment concept appears anywhere in Find in Boutique's documentation, functional or technical.

## Q4 — Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006)

**Confirmed as a requirement; zero technical/library decision on record.**

- **"04.1.13 Gift Cards and Credit Notes"** (id `303693825`, v9, same source Excel):
  - **GC-005**: "The system will display a date picker calendar for the delivery date field, allowing the customer to navigate between months and select a future delivery date." — Status: **Confirmed**
  - **GC-006**: "The system will restrict the delivery date selection to within 3 months from the current date; dates beyond 3 months will be greyed out and unavailable for selection." — Status: **Confirmed**
- **"04.2 Design Tracker"** (id `258801666`) row 16, "Credit Notes & Gift Cards" (Sprint 5): component detail lists *"Gift card PDP (denomination, **date picker**, sender/recipient/message)"* — Design Status **PENDING**, Zimmermann Sign-off **PENDING**. The design for this date picker itself isn't signed off yet either.
- No spike, evaluation, or decision doc anywhere discusses *how* to implement it — no library named, no build-vs-buy note, nothing beyond these two requirement lines and the one tracker row.

**Verdict**: Same "no technical evaluation on record" situation as Q2 — nothing suggests the team already picked (or even discussed) a library here that could be reused for the boutique screen. The trail is cold on both.

## Q5 — Figma-adjacent tech notes for this specific frame

**Nothing found referencing this frame, node-id, or flow by name.**

- No page references node-id `3193-47937` or the "Choose a Date"/"Available Times"/Continue flow.
- **"1.5 Web Design (UX)"** (id `268075023`) — the page that should hold this — is a largely **unfilled template**: placeholder Figma links (`*[link]*`), a blank "Last updated" field, placeholder background-presentation entries, and an explicit closing checklist of things still needed ("A few fill-ins before you publish..."). Its own tracker marks **Phase 2** (which covers My Account/loyalty, and by extension any Appointments sub-area) as **DRAFT — "Not ready for build,"** with only Login/Register slightly further along ("In Review").
- **"04.2 Design Tracker"**'s one relevant row (Loyalty & Appointments, Sprint 4) has an **empty Figma Link cell**, PENDING/PENDING status, and no dev-handoff or feasibility note attached.
- On "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE": I found no dedicated "Angela Lee" persona or test-account page (the "04.3 Personas" page uses generic role-based names). But the Design Tracker's Checkout Entry notes (dated 01-07) show designers instructing generic placeholder copy for an *unrelated* screen: *"If you login as a known customer 'Welcome back, Angela. Email: nnn' and for new users 'Welcome to Zimmermann world, Angela.'"* This suggests "Angela" is a recurring example-customer name the design team reuses across mockups generically, not a signal specific to the appointment flow — but I want to flag this as my own inference from adjacent evidence, not something a page directly confirms.

**Verdict**: This screen sits in a part of Figma that Confluence's own tracking explicitly marks as still in Draft, unsigned-off, and not yet linked into the tracker at all — consistent with no technical decision existing for it yet.

---

## One additional hypothesis worth passing on (my inference, not confirmed by any page)

You noted the Figma layers panel shows this calendar screen grouped under "Find in Boutique" alongside "FIND IN BOUTIQUE modal open" variants. Given every confirmed requirement and the MuleSoft-level TSD are unanimous that Find in Boutique is a stock-check-only flyout with no date/time concept, and given the *actual* appointment feature (Booxi/Booksy, CRM-165–167) is tracked completely separately under "Customer Account & CRM → Loyalty & Appointments" — one plausible explanation is that the designers grouped this screen in Figma by **UI pattern** (both are boutique-related side-out panels) rather than by feature/requirement scope. That would explain why it reads as "under Find in Boutique" visually while actually representing a different, still-undecided feature (Booxi appointment booking, or possibly an entirely new/undocumented concept like a styling or personal-shopping appointment). I could not verify this directly since I don't have Figma access in this session — flagging it only as a hypothesis for whoever synthesizes the final answer.
